topics.name: Surface area of a combination of solids
Volume of a combination of solids

questions.title: Three tennis balls in a jar: volume of air
questions.text: Three tennis balls are just packed in a cylindrical jar. If the radius of each ball is r, the volume of air inside the jar is:
questions.remember:
Balls packed in a jar: jar height = number of balls × diameter.
A ball fills exactly 2/3 of the cylinder around it.
questions.trap: Taking the jar height as 3r. Each ball is 2r tall, so 3 balls need 6r.
questions.tryit: Two balls of radius 3 cm are just packed in a jar. Find the volume of air (in π).

questions.title: Ice-cream cone with two scoops: h : 2r
questions.text: An ice-cream cone of radius r and height h is completely filled by two spherical scoops of ice-cream. If the radius of each spherical scoop is r/2, then h : 2r equals:
questions.remember:
'Completely filled' ⟹ the volumes are EQUAL.
Halve the radius ⟹ the ball's volume becomes 1/8.
questions.trap: Answering h : r = 1 : 1. The question asks h : 2r.
questions.tryit: A cone of radius 3 cm is completely filled by one sphere of radius 3 cm. Find the cone's height.

questions.title: Cap: cylinder + hemisphere, equal volumes
questions.text: A cap is cylindrical in shape and is surmounted by a hemispherical top. If the volume of the cylindrical part is equal to that of the hemispherical part, then the ratio of the height of the cylindrical part to the height of the hemispherical part is :
steps: ④ Height of a hemisphere = r
questions.remember:
A hemisphere's height is its radius r.
Cylinder of height ⅔r = hemisphere of radius r (same volume).
questions.trap: Comparing with the diameter 2r instead of the hemisphere's height r.
questions.tryit: A cylinder and a cone have the same radius and the same volume. Find h(cylinder) : h(cone).

questions.title: Largest cone carved from a 4 cm cube: CSA
questions.text: The curved surface area of the largest right circular cone that can be carved out from a solid cube of edge 4 cm is :
steps: ① Largest cone: base fits the face
questions.remember: Largest cone in a cube of edge a: r = a/2, h = a.
questions.trap: Taking r = 4. The base circle must fit inside the face, so the diameter is 4.
questions.tryit: Find the volume of the largest cone carved from a cube of edge 6 cm (in π).

questions.title: Two cubes joined: surface area
questions.text: Two cubes each of volume 64 cm³ are joined end to end to form a solid. The surface area of the resultant cuboid is:
questions.remember: Joining solids hides the faces that touch. Don't add both full surface areas.
questions.trap: Picking 192 (2 × 96). Two faces are hidden where the cubes join.
questions.tryit: Three cubes of edge 2 cm are joined in a row. Find the surface area.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: two hemispheres make a sphere
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If we join two hemispheres of same radius along their bases, then we get a sphere.
Reason (R): Total Surface Area of a sphere of radius r is 3πr².
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.trap: Picking (a) because 3πr² looks familiar. It's the hemisphere's total, not the sphere's.
questions.tryit: Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm.

questions.title: Room with a dome: find the cylinder's height
questions.text: A room is in the form of a cylinder surmounted by a hemispherical dome. The base radius of the hemisphere is half of the height of the cylindrical part. If the room contains 1408/21 m³ of air, find the height of the cylindrical part. (Use π = 22/7)
steps: ① Radius r ⟹ cylinder height h = 2r
questions.ans: Height of the cylindrical part = 4 m
questions.remember: Volume of a combined solid = add the volumes of its parts.
questions.trap: Using the dome's surface area. Air fills space, so you need VOLUME.
questions.tryit: A cylinder of radius 3 m and height 6 m has a hemispherical dome. Find the total volume (in π).

questions.title: Kajal's lattu: area to colour
questions.text: Kajal got a playing top (lattu) as her birthday gift, which surprisingly had no colour on it. She wanted to colour it with her crayons. The top is shaped like a cone, surmounted by a hemisphere. The entire top is 5 cm in height and the diameter of the top is 3.5 cm. Find the area she has to colour. [Use π = 22/7]
questions.remember: Coloured / painted / covered ⟹ SURFACE area of the outside only.
questions.trap: Adding the flat circle where the cone meets the dome. It is inside the toy.
questions.tryit: A toy: hemisphere of radius 7 cm on a cone of slant height 25 cm. Find its total surface area.

questions.title: The green-cloth shed: area of cloth
questions.text: To protect plants from heat, a shed of iron rods covered with green cloth is made. The lower part of the shed is a cuboid, with a half-cylinder (semi-cylinder) on top, its diameter equal to the cuboid's width. The cuboid is 25 m long, 14 m wide and 16 m high. Find the area of cloth required to make the shed (no cloth on the floor).
steps: ① Cloth: 4 walls + curved roof + 2 ends
questions.remember: Surface-area problems: list only the faces you can touch from outside, then add.
questions.trap: Adding the floor or the cuboid's top. The roof covers the top, and the floor needs no cloth.
questions.tryit: A half-cylinder roof has radius 3.5 m and length 10 m. Find its curved area.

questions.title: The tent: canvas area and cost (5 marks)
questions.text: A tent is in the shape of a cylinder surmounted by a conical top. If the height and radius of the cylindrical part are 3 m and 14 m respectively, and the total height of the tent is 13.5 m, then find the area of the canvas required for making the tent, keeping a provision of 26 m² of canvas for stitching and wastage. Also, find the cost of the canvas to be purchased at the rate of ₹ 250 per m².
questions.remember: Tent canvas = cylinder's curved wall (2πrh) + cone's curved top (πrl). No floor, no base circles.
questions.trap: Using the total height 13.5 m as the cone's height. Subtract the 3 m cylinder first.
questions.tryit: Cone: radius 7 m, height 24 m. Find its slant height.
